name: Osmium Reservations
description: Table reservation requests the restaurant confirms or declines: tables with seats, party size, opening hours with a break between lunch and dinner, a hidden dining time and turnaround, a Live schedule, drag a booking to another table or time (with an email/text prompt), an Arrived step that locks the table, optional automatic answers that book a free table at once and email the nearest free times when full, emails and calendar links, with hooks so a calendar service can follow along

setup.postInstallNote: Under Content > Osmium Reservations add the tables (name and seats) and set the booking rules: dining time (how long a table is held, never shown to customers), smallest and largest party, notice, how far ahead and who is emailed. Opening hours come from Company > Location. The service ships no form: a theme builds one that posts to /api/reservations (with a trailing slash if the site uses them) with the fields party_size, date (YYYY-MM-DD), time (HH:MM), name, email, phone (optional), notes (optional), the form token and the empty zip honeypot, and reads what it needs from $reservations = new \Osmium\Services\OsmiumReservations\Models\Reservations($this->osmium->dataSource): rules() and pullNotice() (status sent or failed, and a message, shown once). Requests are emailed to the customer and to the addresses in the settings; the owner confirms or declines in the admin, and confirming gives the booking the smallest free table that fits. A confirmed reservation's email links to Google Calendar and to an .ics file. Other services follow along through the hooks reservation.requested, reservation.confirmed, reservation.changed, reservation.declined and reservation.cancelled (payload: reservation, reservationId, dataSource, osmium).
